_meta.note: PLACEHOLDER / DUMMY DATA for Phase 1 demo only. Generated from general botanical knowledge, not verified per-source. Gujarati names, exact coordinates, and area names MUST be replaced with the professor's real dataset before any real deployment.

trees.native_status: Native to South Asia; cultivated across India for over 4,000 years
trees.description: A large evergreen tree grown widely across India, prized above all for its fruit. Gujarat's Kutch and Saurashtra regions grow well-known mango varieties such as Kesar.
trees.uses: The ripe fruit is eaten fresh or used in juices and desserts; raw mango is used in pickles and chutneys; leaves are used in some religious décor.
trees.wood_quality: Medium-hard wood, sometimes used for cheap furniture and packing crates, but the tree is grown for fruit, not timber.
trees.flowering_season: January to March, with fruit ripening April to June
trees.fun_fact: The mango is India's national fruit, and India is the world's largest producer.
trees.fruiting_season: April to June (varies by cultivar; Alphonso April-June, Kesar May-July)
trees.co2_sequestration: ~30-50 kg CO2/year (estimated; Indian mango-orchard studies found a per-tree range of ~30-78 kg CO2/year, averaging ~50 kg)
trees.useful_parts: Fruit, Bark, Leaves, Wood, Seed kernel
trees.avg_lifespan: 100-300 years (commercially productive for roughly the first 40-80 years)

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A massive, long-living tree known for aerial roots that descend from its branches and thicken into secondary trunks, letting one tree spread over a huge area.
trees.uses: Widely regarded as sacred in Indian tradition; provides deep shade and is a common gathering point in villages; bark and leaves used in traditional remedies.
trees.wood_quality: Soft, not valued as timber; the tree's importance is ecological and cultural, not for wood.
trees.flowering_season: Produces small figs nearly year-round rather than showy flowers
trees.fun_fact: India's national tree; a single banyan in Kolkata's botanical garden covers several acres.
trees.fruiting_season: Figs ripen year-round, with a peak around spring
trees.co2_sequestration: Estimates vary widely (~25 to 500+ kg CO2/year, estimated) because mature banyans spread via aerial prop roots and can have far greater biomass than a typical single-trunk tree of similar height; ~25-50 kg CO2/year is a reasonable estimate for a young-to-medium specimen
trees.useful_parts: Bark, Leaves, Aerial roots, Latex, Fruit (wildlife food), Wood
trees.avg_lifespan: 200-500 years commonly; some famous individuals (which keep renewing via prop roots) are reported at 1,000+ years

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A large fig tree with distinctive heart-shaped, long-tipped leaves that shimmer in the wind. Considered sacred in Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism.
trees.uses: Associated with religious worship; leaves and bark used in traditional remedies; commonly planted near temples.
trees.wood_quality: Soft and not commonly used as structural timber.
trees.flowering_season: Inconspicuous flowers inside its figs, produced through much of the year
trees.fun_fact: Buddhist tradition holds that Buddha attained enlightenment while sitting under a peepal tree.
trees.fruiting_season: May to June (flowers in February; new leaves in April)
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated for a mature tree; sources range roughly 20-40 kg/year)
trees.useful_parts: Bark, Leaves, Fruit, Roots (all used in traditional medicine); heart-shaped leaves also used ceremonially
trees.avg_lifespan: 900-1,500 years on average; some specimens in native habitats reportedly exceed 3,000 years

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A fast-growing, hardy, drought-tolerant tree with feathery leaves, common in home gardens and roadsides across India.
trees.uses: Traditionally used for skin conditions and as a natural pest repellent; leaves stored with grain and clothes to deter insects; twigs traditionally used as a natural toothbrush.
trees.wood_quality: Moderately hard, termite-resistant wood, used in some furniture and construction.
trees.fun_fact: Neem is sometimes called the 'village pharmacy' in rural India for its many traditional uses.
trees.fruiting_season: June to August (fruit ripens ~12 weeks after flowering; flowering mainly April-May and again August-September in some regions)
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated for a medium-sized tree)
trees.useful_parts: Leaves, Bark, Seeds, Oil, Fruit, Twigs
trees.avg_lifespan: 150-200 years

trees.native_status: Native to Madagascar; widely naturalised and planted across India
trees.description: A striking ornamental tree with a broad, flat-topped canopy and brilliant red-orange flowers that cover the tree in summer.
trees.uses: Grown almost entirely for shade and ornamental value along avenues and parks; not typically used for food or medicine.
trees.wood_quality: Soft and brittle; not used as structural timber.
trees.fun_fact: It's called the 'Flame of the Forest' in many countries for how vividly it blooms.
trees.fruiting_season: Pods form after the April-June flowering flush and mature by winter (roughly October to December)
trees.co2_sequestration: Species-specific annual rate not well documented; as a fast-growing medium-sized tree, ~20-30 kg CO2/year is a reasonable general estimate (biomass studies do rank Delonix regia among the higher carbon-stock urban trees in India)
trees.useful_parts: Wood, Bark, Flowers, Seeds; valued mainly for ornamental shade rather than fruit/timber use
trees.avg_lifespan: 40-60 years

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A small to medium evergreen tree with dense, dark green foliage and fragrant orange-yellow flower clusters, often planted near temples.
trees.uses: Considered sacred and associated with several Indian legends; bark traditionally used in Ayurvedic preparations for women's health.
trees.wood_quality: Not typically used as timber; valued as an ornamental and sacred tree.
trees.fun_fact: Often confused with the unrelated 'Mast Tree' (Polyalthia longifolia), which is sometimes sold as 'false ashoka.'
trees.fruiting_season: Fruit matures May to July (flowering December to May, peaking February-March)
trees.co2_sequestration: Not well documented for this species; as a small-to-medium evergreen tree, ~15-20 kg CO2/year is a reasonable estimate based on general averages for trees of similar size
trees.useful_parts: Bark, Flowers, Seeds (used in Ayurvedic medicine); flowers also used ceremonially
trees.avg_lifespan: 50-100 years (polycarpic, flowering repeatedly through its life)
trees.pollinator: Bees (including carpenter bees) and other insects attracted to the bright flower colour

trees.native_status: Likely native to tropical Africa, naturalised in India for centuries
trees.description: A long-lived, slow-growing tree with feathery leaves and a dense canopy, producing curved brown pods with sour-sweet pulp.
trees.uses: Pulp used extensively in Indian cooking (chutneys, sambhar, candies); also used in traditional remedies for digestion.
trees.wood_quality: Very hard, heavy, and durable wood, used for furniture, tool handles, and wood carving.
trees.fun_fact: A single tamarind tree can live for well over 100 years and keep fruiting.
trees.fruiting_season: Flowers April to June; pods ripen by winter (roughly December to February)
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20 kg CO2/year (estimated); one Indian urban-forestry study measured cumulative carbon storage of ~1,667 kg C in a mature tamarind tree
trees.useful_parts: Fruit pulp, Seeds, Leaves, Flowers, Bark, Wood
trees.avg_lifespan: 60-200 years (some specimens reportedly reach 300 years)

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia
trees.description: A dense evergreen tree producing dark purple, tangy-sweet fruit in summer, common along roadsides and in orchards.
trees.uses: Fruit eaten fresh or used in juices and vinegar; seeds are traditionally used in home remedies related to blood sugar.
trees.wood_quality: Moderately hard, water-resistant wood, sometimes used for well construction and boats.
trees.flowering_season: March to April, fruiting May to July
trees.fun_fact: Jamun-stained tongues are a childhood memory for many people who grew up near these trees in India.
trees.fruiting_season: May to June, harvested through the monsoon (June-July)
trees.co2_sequestration: Species-specific figure not well documented; as a large, dense-canopy evergreen tree (up to 30 m), ~25-30 kg CO2/year is a reasonable estimate based on similar-sized tree averages
trees.useful_parts: Fruit, Seeds, Bark, Leaves, Wood
trees.avg_lifespan: Over 100 years

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A small to medium deciduous tree with feathery leaves and small, round, translucent green fruit known for its sharp sourness.
trees.uses: Fruit used in pickles, candies, and traditional preparations like chyawanprash; widely used in Ayurveda.
trees.wood_quality: Moderately hard wood, occasionally used for small implements and fuelwood.
trees.fun_fact: Amla is considered one of the richest natural sources of vitamin C among common fruits.
trees.fruiting_season: June to September (ripe fruit can remain on the tree for several months without spoiling)
trees.co2_sequestration: Not well documented; as a small-to-medium deciduous tree, ~15-20 kg CO2/year is a reasonable estimate based on general averages for trees of similar size
trees.useful_parts: Fruit, Seeds, Leaves, Bark, Roots, Flowers
trees.avg_lifespan: Productive fruiting for 50+ years; individual trees can live considerably longer
trees.pollination_method: Mixed: Entomophily and Anemophily (both insect- and wind-assisted)
trees.pollinator: Bees and other small insects, with some wind pollination

trees.native_status: Native to the Western Ghats region of India
trees.description: A large tropical tree producing the largest tree-borne fruit in the world, growing directly from the trunk and thick branches.
trees.uses: Ripe fruit eaten fresh or used in desserts; raw/young jackfruit widely used as a meat substitute in curries.
trees.wood_quality: Durable, termite-resistant, golden-hued wood, valued for furniture and musical instruments.
trees.flowering_season: Flowers most of the year; main fruiting season March to July
trees.fun_fact: A single jackfruit can weigh over 30 kilograms.
trees.fruiting_season: Summer to early autumn (roughly March to September depending on region); fruit matures 150-180 days after flowering
trees.co2_sequestration: Not precisely documented per tree; comparative studies rank jackfruit among the stronger carbon-sequestering fruit trees given its large size and dense biomass (one regional study found jackfruit stands storing ~26.7 tonnes CO2/hectare). A reasonable per-tree estimate is ~30-40 kg CO2/year
trees.useful_parts: Fruit, Seeds, Leaves (fodder), Wood, Latex
trees.avg_lifespan: 50-100 years (over 100 years reported in some cases)
trees.pollination_method: Mixed: Entomophily and Anemophily (insects and wind both involved)
trees.pollinator: Insects (attracted to scented male flowers), with wind dispersing pollen to female flowers

trees.native_status: Likely native to the Indo-Pacific coastal region; common along India's coastline
trees.description: A tall palm with a slender curved trunk and a crown of large feathery leaves, closely associated with coastal India.
trees.uses: Water, flesh, and oil used widely in cooking; every part of the tree is traditionally used, giving it the nickname 'tree of life'; leaves used for thatching and religious rituals.
trees.wood_quality: Fibrous 'wood' from the trunk is used in some construction; not a hardwood timber.
trees.flowering_season: Flowers and fruits nearly year-round once mature
trees.fun_fact: A single coconut palm can produce fruit for over 60 years.
trees.fruiting_season: Year-round in the tropics; ~11-12 months from flower opening to harvest, with a seasonal peak after the dry period
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated, general medium-large tree average) - no reliable per-tree figure found; plantation-level studies report ~12-13 tonnes carbon/ha/year sequestered in coconut stands
trees.useful_parts: Fruit (meat, water), Husk, Shell, Leaves, Trunk/wood, Roots
trees.avg_lifespan: 60-100 years (tall varieties); dwarf varieties are shorter-lived but bear earlier
trees.pollination_method: Mixed: anemophily (wind) and entomophily (insects); tall varieties are predominantly cross-pollinated, dwarf varieties mostly self-pollinated
trees.pollinator: Wind (primary agent in tall varieties); insects also visit; self-pollination common in dwarf varieties

trees.native_status: Native to South and Southeast Asia, including central India
trees.description: A tall deciduous tree with very large, rough leaves, grown commercially across India for its valuable timber.
trees.uses: Almost entirely grown for timber rather than food or medicine; occasionally leaves are used as natural plate liners in rural areas.
trees.wood_quality: One of the most valued hardwoods in the world — strong, naturally weather- and pest-resistant, prized for furniture, boats, and construction.
trees.fun_fact: Teak furniture can last for generations without needing chemical preservatives, thanks to natural oils in the wood.
trees.fruiting_season: September to December (fruit sets after June-August flowering)
trees.co2_sequestration: Reported among the highest of Indian timber species; plantations estimated to sequester ~191 tonnes CO2/ha over a 20-year rotation (study-based estimate, not a simple per-tree annual figure)
trees.useful_parts: Wood (timber, furniture), Leaves (natural dye, plates), Bark, Flowers
trees.avg_lifespan: 80-150+ years
trees.pollinator: Bees (notably Ceratina spp. recorded in Thailand studies), other insects

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent, mainly central and eastern India
trees.description: A tall, straight-trunked tree forming vast forests across central India, with broad leathery leaves.
trees.uses: Resin traditionally used as incense; leaves used to make disposable eco-friendly plates; historically significant in tribal and religious contexts.
trees.wood_quality: Very strong, durable hardwood, historically used for railway sleepers and heavy construction.
trees.fun_fact: Buddhist tradition holds that Buddha was born under a sal tree.
trees.fruiting_season: May to July (fruit ripens and disperses April to June)
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated, general medium-to-large tree average) - no species-specific published figure found
trees.useful_parts: Resin (dhoop/damar), Seeds (sal oil), Leaves (plates/bowls), Wood (timber), Bark
trees.avg_lifespan: 100-200 years in natural forest; commercial rotations of 30-160 years depending on regeneration method (coppice vs. high forest)

trees.native_status: Native to Central America; widely naturalised and planted across India
trees.description: A small ornamental tree with thick, waxy branches and highly fragrant white or yellow flowers.
trees.uses: Flowers widely used in religious offerings and garlands; essential oils used in perfumery.
trees.wood_quality: Soft wood with little structural use, sometimes used in minor carving.
trees.fun_fact: Its fragrance is strongest at night, when it attracts pollinating moths.
trees.fruiting_season: Seed pods rarely form (plants mostly propagated by cuttings); when they do, pods mature in early spring following flowers from June to November
trees.co2_sequestration: ~15-20 kg CO2/year (estimated; small-to-medium ornamental tree, below large-canopy-tree averages) - not well documented for this species
trees.useful_parts: Flowers (fragrance, perfume, incense), Bark and sap (traditional medicine), Latex, Leaves
trees.avg_lifespan: 50-100 years (estimated) - reaches full size in ~5 years and is long-lived, but a precise documented maximum age was not found
trees.pollination_method: Entomophily (insect-pollinated), via deceptive pollination (flowers are scented but offer no nectar reward)

trees.native_status: Native to Australia; commonly planted ornamentally in India
trees.description: A small tree or large shrub named for its brush-shaped red flower spikes that resemble a bottle-cleaning brush.
trees.uses: Almost entirely ornamental; flowers attract birds and bees; occasionally used in traditional Australian remedies.
trees.wood_quality: Hard but rarely used commercially; the tree is grown for looks, not timber.
trees.flowering_season: March to June, sometimes again in autumn
trees.fun_fact: Its flowers are rich in nectar and are a favourite of sunbirds in Indian gardens.
trees.fruiting_season: Summer to autumn, following flowering (in India: chiefly February-May and August-November)
trees.co2_sequestration: ~10-15 kg CO2/year (estimated; small-to-medium shrub/tree, below large-tree averages) - not well documented for this species
trees.useful_parts: Leaves (tea substitute, dye source), Flowers (dye), Wood (tool handles)
trees.avg_lifespan: ~50 years (medium lifespan reported for the species)
trees.pollinator: Honeyeaters and other nectar-feeding birds; bees and other insects

trees.native_status: Native to Central and South America; widely planted as a shade tree across India
trees.description: A very large, wide-canopied tree valued almost entirely for the deep, umbrella-like shade it casts.
trees.uses: Primarily an avenue and shade tree; pods are sometimes used as cattle fodder.
trees.wood_quality: Moderately soft wood, occasionally used for carving and lightweight furniture.
trees.fun_fact: Its leaves fold up in the evening or before rain, which is how it earned the name 'rain tree.'
trees.fruiting_season: Fruits mature 5.5-8 months after flowering; main crop ripens February to May
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated, general large-tree average) - no species-specific figure found; being nitrogen-fixing and fast-growing with a very wide canopy, actual sequestration may run higher
trees.useful_parts: Pods (livestock fodder), Wood (furniture, carving - 'monkeypod'), Bark, Leaves (fodder, green manure)
trees.avg_lifespan: 80-100+ years
trees.pollinator: Bees and butterflies; also sparrows and hummingbirds drawn to abundant nectar
trees.image_source: Wikimedia Commons (famous specimen, Moanalua Gardens, Hawaii)

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia
trees.description: A medium-sized tree with glossy leaves, commonly planted along roads and coastlines for its tolerance of poor soil.
trees.uses: Seed oil traditionally used in lamps and skin treatments, and increasingly studied as a biodiesel source; leaves used as a natural pest deterrent.
trees.wood_quality: Moderately hard wood, used for low-cost furniture and fuelwood.
trees.fun_fact: Karanj oil is one of the earliest biodiesel candidates researched in India.
trees.fruiting_season: April to October, with pods developing to full size June to September
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-30 kg CO2/year for a mature tree (estimate reported in biofuel/agroforestry literature; varies with growth conditions)
trees.useful_parts: Seeds/oil (biodiesel, lubricant, soap), Leaves (green manure), Bark (fibre for rope), Wood
trees.avg_lifespan: Productive for several decades (starts bearing year 4-6); precise maximum natural lifespan not well documented, commonly cited informally as 50-100 years
trees.pollinator: Bees (nectar-feeding, trigger pollen release from keel petals)

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A medium tree with spines and aromatic leaves in groups of three, producing a hard-shelled, fragrant fruit.
trees.uses: Fruit pulp used to make a traditional cooling summer drink; leaves considered sacred in Shiva worship; used in traditional digestive remedies.
trees.wood_quality: Hard, yellowish wood, occasionally used for tool handles.
trees.fun_fact: Bael leaves are traditionally offered in threes during worship of Lord Shiva.
trees.fruiting_season: July-August harvest; fruit takes 10-11 months to ripen from April-May flowering, maturing March-June of the following year
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated, general medium-tree average) - not well documented for this species
trees.useful_parts: Fruit (pulp, juice, murabba), Leaves (medicinal, ritual use), Bark, Root, Wood
trees.avg_lifespan: 50-100 years (estimated) - a slow-growing tree with a long productive life; precise documented maximum age not found
trees.pollination_method: Entomophily (insect-pollinated); self-incompatible, requiring cross-pollination for fruit set

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A tall, thorny-trunked tree that loses its leaves before bursting into large, striking red flowers.
trees.uses: Seed floss traditionally used as pillow and mattress stuffing; gum used in some traditional remedies.
trees.wood_quality: Soft, lightweight wood, used for packing cases, matchsticks, and plywood.
trees.flowering_season: January to March, typically while leafless
trees.fun_fact: Its cotton-like seed floss is naturally water-resistant, which is why it was historically used in life jackets.
trees.fruiting_season: March to May (fruit develops rapidly, often still forming while flowers remain on the leafless tree)
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated, general medium-large tree average) - not well documented for this species; it is a fast-growing tree, which may favour higher early sequestration
trees.useful_parts: Fibre/kapok (fruit floss, used for stuffing), Gum (bark secretion, medicinal), Flowers (edible, medicinal), Roots, Bark
trees.avg_lifespan: Reaches ~30 m height and 2-3 m girth in about 50 years; can live considerably longer, though a precise maximum age is not well documented
trees.pollination_method: Ornithophily (bird-pollinated), with entomophily as a secondary pathway
trees.pollinator: Birds (mynas, sunbirds and others drawn to the bright red flowers); honeybees and bumblebees

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A large tree with a distinctive smooth, pale, buttressed trunk, often found along riverbanks.
trees.uses: Bark widely used in traditional Ayurvedic preparations, particularly ones associated with heart health.
trees.wood_quality: Hard, strong wood, used for agricultural tools and construction.
trees.fun_fact: Its smooth, pale bark makes it easy to identify even from a distance.
trees.fruiting_season: September to November (flowering March to June/July)
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated, general large-tree average) - no species-specific figure found; its notably dense wood may support above-average carbon storage per unit volume
trees.useful_parts: Bark (cardiotonic, widely used in Ayurveda), Leaves (fodder, tanning), Fruit (tanning), Wood
trees.avg_lifespan: Commonly exceeds 50 years and frequently over 100 years
trees.pollinator: Honeybees - the tree is a major nectar source for honey production in parts of Kerala and Karnataka

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia
trees.description: A tall evergreen tree with leaves arranged in whorls of seven (giving it its name), and clusters of strongly scented small flowers.
trees.uses: Bark traditionally used in remedies for fever; wood historically used for writing slates and school blackboards.
trees.wood_quality: Soft, lightweight wood, easy to work but not very durable.
trees.fun_fact: Its heavy night-time fragrance means some cities restrict planting it directly outside homes.
trees.fruiting_season: January to April (flowers October-December, fruits follow)
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated, based on medium-to-large tree averages; no species-specific figure found in literature)
trees.useful_parts: Bark, Latex, Leaves, Wood
trees.avg_lifespan: 40-60 years (estimated; precise figure not well documented, but it is a large, fast-growing tree reaching 40 m)
trees.pollination_method: Entomophily (insect-pollinated, with floral traits adapted for moths); also self-compatible/self-pollinating

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A tall, narrow, columnar evergreen tree with long drooping leaves, very commonly planted along roads and as a privacy screen.
trees.uses: Almost entirely ornamental and used for noise/dust screening along roads; not the same species as the sacred true Ashoka tree, despite the common name.
trees.wood_quality: Lightweight wood, historically used for ship masts, giving the tree its English name.
trees.fun_fact: It's frequently mislabelled simply as 'Ashoka tree,' though it's botanically unrelated to Saraca asoca.
trees.fruiting_season: Summer to autumn (fruit ripens dark purple-black after February-April flowering)
trees.co2_sequestration: Not well documented as an annual rate; a campus study in India found ~302 kg of carbon sequestered per tree cumulatively (timeframe/age unspecified). For an annual estimate, ~20-25 kg CO2/year is typical for a medium tree (estimated)
trees.useful_parts: Wood, Bark, Leaves
trees.avg_lifespan: Not well documented; estimated 20-40 years for cultivated avenue/ornamental specimens (moderately slow-growing, reaching 10-18 m)

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A medium tree that turns forests orange-red when its brilliant flowers bloom on otherwise bare branches.
trees.uses: Flowers traditionally used to make natural dye (associated with the Holi festival); gum and bark used in some traditional remedies.
trees.wood_quality: Soft, spongy wood, not commercially valuable as timber.
trees.fun_fact: Its flowers are the traditional source of the natural orange-red colour once used in Holi celebrations.
trees.fruiting_season: May to June (woody pods mature after February-April flowering)
trees.co2_sequestration: Not well documented as an annual rate; a Maharashtra campus study recorded ~3.55 tonnes cumulative carbon sequestered per tree (age/timeframe unspecified). For an annual estimate, ~20-25 kg CO2/year is typical for a medium tree (estimated)
trees.useful_parts: Flowers (dye), Gum/resin, Bark, Leaves, Lac (as host tree)
trees.avg_lifespan: 40-100 years (estimated; described as long-living but precise figures not well documented)

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A medium to large deciduous tree with a light, airy canopy, widely planted along roads and canal banks.
trees.uses: Grown mainly for its valuable timber; leaves sometimes used as fodder.
trees.wood_quality: One of India's most prized timbers — strong, richly grained, and widely used in furniture making.
trees.fun_fact: Shisham furniture is a mainstay of Indian carpentry and is often exported internationally.
trees.fruiting_season: April to May (pods persist on tree for 7-8 months)
trees.co2_sequestration: ~22 kg CO2/year for a mature individual tree (estimated); plantation studies report ~7.56 t/ha carbon sequestration capacity
trees.useful_parts: Wood/Timber, Leaves (fodder), Bark
trees.avg_lifespan: Over 100 years with proper growing conditions
trees.pollination_method: Entomophily (insect-pollinated); capable of both self- and cross-pollination

trees.native_status: Native to arid regions of the Indian subcontinent, especially Rajasthan and Kutch
trees.description: A slow-growing, deeply-rooted tree that thrives in hot, dry, and saline soils where few other trees survive.
trees.uses: Pods (sangri) used in traditional desert cuisine; leaves used as fodder during droughts; considered central to desert ecology and livelihoods.
trees.wood_quality: Hard, durable wood, used for farm tools, fuelwood, and construction in arid regions.
trees.fun_fact: It's the state tree of Rajasthan and central to the story of the Chipko-like Khejarli sacrifice in 1730.
trees.fruiting_season: April to June (pods reach full size about two months after mid-April to mid-May flowering)
trees.co2_sequestration: Not well documented as a per-tree annual rate; agroforestry studies rank Khejri among the most efficient carbon sinks of arid-zone trees (plantations reported up to ~106 Mg C/ha). For a single-tree annual estimate, ~20-25 kg CO2/year is typical for a medium tree (estimated)
trees.useful_parts: Pods, Leaves (fodder), Bark, Wood
trees.avg_lifespan: 150-200+ years (some individual specimens, e.g. in desert regions, reach ~400 years)
trees.pollinator: Honey bees (Apis cerana indica, A. dorsata), wasps, lady bird beetles

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, and Africa
trees.description: A thorny, hardy tree common across dry parts of Gujarat, with feathery leaves and small round yellow flower clusters.
trees.uses: Bark and gum traditionally used in tanning and some remedies; twigs traditionally used as a natural toothbrush.
trees.wood_quality: Very hard, durable wood, used for tool handles, fencing, and fuelwood.
trees.fun_fact: Its gum (gum arabic-like resin) has traditionally been used as a natural adhesive and thickener.
trees.fruiting_season: Pods form after spring flowering and mature through summer (precise regional timing not well documented)
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated, based on medium-sized tree averages; no species-specific figure found)
trees.useful_parts: Bark, Gum, Pods, Wood
trees.avg_lifespan: 30-60 years

trees.native_status: Native to Australia and the Pacific; widely planted along Indian coastlines
trees.description: A tall, slender, pine-like tree with fine, needle-like branchlets, often planted in dense coastal rows.
trees.uses: Widely planted as a windbreak and to stabilise coastal soil; wood used as fuelwood and pulp.
trees.wood_quality: Hard, dense wood, but not typically used for fine furniture.
trees.flowering_season: Inconspicuous flowers through much of the year
trees.fun_fact: Despite looking like a pine, it isn't a conifer at all — it's a flowering plant.
trees.fruiting_season: Flowers and fruits year-round in warm climates, often with two peaks (February-April and September-October); cones mature ~18-20 weeks after flowering
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated, based on fast-growing medium-sized tree averages; no species-specific figure found)
trees.useful_parts: Wood, Bark, Leaves/needles
trees.avg_lifespan: 40-50 years

trees.native_status: Native to Australia; widely planted in India for timber and pulp
trees.description: A tall, fast-growing tree with aromatic leaves and distinctive peeling bark, common in plantation rows.
trees.uses: Leaves and oil used in traditional decongestant remedies; wood used for pulp, plywood, and construction poles.
trees.wood_quality: Moderately hard, fast-grown wood, mainly valued for pulp and construction rather than fine furniture.
trees.flowering_season: Varies by species and region, often winter to spring
trees.fun_fact: Its strong-smelling oil is a common ingredient in cold and cough balms.
trees.fruiting_season: Autumn (woody capsule 'gum-nut' fruits follow flowering, which in India occurs roughly September-December)
trees.co2_sequestration: Indian plantation studies report ~6-11 Mg C/ha/year at stand level; for a single mature tree, ~25-30 kg CO2/year is a reasonable estimate given its fast growth rate (estimated, species-specific single-tree figure not well documented)
trees.useful_parts: Leaves (oil), Bark, Wood
trees.avg_lifespan: Can exceed 100 years in its native range; commercial plantations are typically harvested at 10-20 years
trees.pollination_method: Entomophily (insect-pollinated, predominantly by bees); wind plays only a minor role
trees.pollinator: Honey bees (primary); also birds and small mammals

trees.native_status: Native to the Indian subcontinent
trees.description: A medium tree that produces cascading chains of bright yellow flowers, blooming vividly in the peak of summer.
trees.uses: Pod pulp traditionally used as a mild laxative in Ayurveda; widely planted for ornamental avenue value.
trees.wood_quality: Hard, durable wood, occasionally used for tool handles and construction posts.
trees.fun_fact: It's the national flower of Thailand and the state flower of Kerala.
trees.fruiting_season: Pods develop after April-May flowering, ripening to black over several months
trees.co2_sequestration: ~20-25 kg CO2/year (estimated, based on medium-sized tree averages; no species-specific figure found)
trees.useful_parts: Fruit pulp, Pods, Bark, Root, Leaves, Flowers
trees.avg_lifespan: 30-50 years (estimated; described as long-lived but precise figures not well documented)
